Standard Library > fmt: Number and Byte Formatting

fmt: Number and Byte Formatting

This page lists the extern functions in sa_std/fmt.sai: formatting i64 / u64 / f64 / bool / byte sequences into text. After reading it, you will be able to choose between the “allocate a buffer” and “write into an existing buffer” forms, and release the returned handle correctly.

Two Forms

The sa_fmt_* series returns an owned buffer handle (u64), which must be freed with sa_fmt_buffer_free after use; the sa_fmt_*_into series writes the result into a buffer supplied by the caller, which suits small on-stack buffers and zero allocation.

Allocating Form (Returns a Buffer Handle)

SignatureDescription
sa_fmt_i64(value: i64, base: u32) -> u64Format a signed integer in the given base (e.g. 10, 16)
sa_fmt_u64(value: u64, base: u32) -> u64Format an unsigned integer in the given base
sa_fmt_f64(value: f64, precision: u32) -> u64Format a floating-point number at the specified precision
sa_fmt_bool(value: i1) -> u64Format a boolean value
sa_fmt_bytes(&buf: ptr, len: u64) -> u64Convert a byte buffer to printable text

Writing Form (into Variants)

SignatureDescription
sa_fmt_i64_into(value: i64, base: u32, out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32Format into out; the actual length is written to out_len
sa_fmt_u64_into(value: u64, base: u32, out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32Same as above, unsigned version
sa_fmt_f64_into(value: f64, precision: u32, out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32Same as above, floating-point version
sa_fmt_bool_into(value: i1, out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32Same as above, boolean version
sa_fmt_bytes_into(&buf: ptr, len: u64, out: ptr, out_cap: u64, &out_len: ptr) -> i32Same as above, byte version

Buffer Handle Accessors

SignatureDescription
sa_fmt_buffer_data(buffer: u64) -> &ptrGet the buffer data pointer (borrowed)
sa_fmt_buffer_len(buffer: u64) -> u64Get the number of bytes in the buffer
sa_fmt_buffer_write_to(buffer: u64, writer: u64) -> i32Write the buffer contents to a writer handle
sa_fmt_buffer_free(^buffer: u64) -> i32Release an owned buffer

The Experience on the Sla Side

Sla code usually does not need to call these functions directly: the placeholder expansion of println("{}", x) is done by the compiler, with the fmt contract underneath. From demos/rosetta/04_loop/main.sla:

println("[{},{},{},{}]", zeroed[0], zeroed[1], zeroed[2], zeroed[3]);

Only when you need non-decimal output or precise control over floating-point precision do you import and call a function such as sa_fmt_u64(v, 16) directly.

NoteThe parameter order differs between the allocating and writing forms: in an into variant, the value is immediately followed by the three buffer parameters out / out_cap / &out_len, so it is easy to forget the capacity when mixing the two forms.
